mainTopic: The creation of חוה, rules of צניעות in walking behind a woman, and a series of aggadic sayings of רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר
overview: This amud is a long chain of aggadic teachings. It begins by finishing a דרשה on ויבן: חוה was built like a storehouse, wide below so she can carry a child. From ויביאה אל האדם we learn that הקב"ה served as אדם's שושבין, so a great person should serve a lesser one. רב נחמן בר יצחק says that on the פרצוף view the man walked in front, and he brings a ברייתא forbidding a man to walk behind a woman. A related ברייתא warns that handing money to a woman as an excuse to gaze at her leads to the judgment of גיהנם. רב נחמן calls מנוח an עם הארץ for walking after his wife. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that 'after her' means following her advice, as with אלקנה and אלישע, and רבי יוחנן then ranks what one should not walk behind. The rest of the amud is a series of sayings of רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר. They cover אדם fathering demons, with a challenge from רבי מאיר and its answer, partial praise to a person's face, the dove's olive leaf, תורה at night protecting a home, the two-letter Name יה after the חורבן, and the curses of בבל and שומרון. The proof about שומרון continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Woman is built like a storehouse
steps.stepSummary: The דרשה on ויבן concludes: just as a storehouse is wide at the bottom to hold produce, a woman is wide at the bottom to carry a child.
steps.simpleTranslation: [He built her like] a storehouse. Just as a storehouse is wide at the bottom and narrow at the top so it can hold produce, a woman is also wide at the bottom and narrow at the top so she can carry a baby.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of a sentence. The גמרא is finishing its explanation of why the תורה says the הקב"ה "built" (ויבן) the rib into a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ויבן is a building word, so the דרשה compares חוה's body to a building, specifically an אוצר (storehouse). A storehouse is wide below so it can carry weight without collapsing. The woman's body is designed the same way, so that it can carry a pregnancy.
steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts mid-sentence. The opening word אוצר is the end of a sentence from the previous page that explained the word ויבן ("and He built").

phrases.english: [like] a storehouse; just as this storehouse
phrases.notes: Continues the explanation of ויבן from the previous page

phrases.english: is wide at the bottom and narrow at the top
in order to hold the produce
so too the woman is wide at the bottom
and narrow at the top
in order to hold the child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a דרשה begun on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word ויבן teaches that the woman was built like a storehouse, wide below so she can carry a child.

steps.title: The הקב"ה served as אדם's best man
steps.stepSummary: From ויביאה אל האדם we learn that the הקב"ה acted as שושבין for אדם הראשון. From this we learn that a great person should serve a lesser person this way without feeling it is beneath him.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And He brought her to the man": this teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, acted as best man for the first man. From here we learn that a great person should serve as best man for a lesser person and should not feel bad about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the same פסוק. It learns a lesson in humility from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Personally bringing the bride to the groom is the role of the שושבין (best man). Since the הקב"ה Himself did this for אדם, a person of high stature has no excuse to feel that serving a lesser person is beneath his dignity.

keyTerms.meaning: "And He brought her to the man" (בראשית ב:כב)
Serving as a best man who attends to the wedding needs
And he should not feel bad about it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the middah of humility. Even an important person should help and honor those beneath him.

phrases.english: "And He brought her to the man"
teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, acted
as best man for the first man
from here [we learn] that a great person should act
as best man for a lesser person
and he should not feel bad about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expounds the next words of the same פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הקב"ה was אדם's שושבין, so a great person should serve a lesser one without resentment.

steps.title: Who walked in front, אדם or חוה?
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that חוה was originally a פרצוף (a full side of אדם), the גמרא asks which of the two walked in front.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says she was a "face" (a full side), which one of them walked in front?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question based on an opinion mentioned earlier. It is setting up רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier there was a dispute about whether the צלע was a פרצוף (a whole second face or side) or just a זנב (a tail). If אדם and חוה were originally one being with two faces, then once they were separated it is not obvious who should go first. The גמרא wants to know which one led.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
A face; here, a full second side of אדם

phrases.english: And according to the one who says [she was] a face,
which one of them walked in front?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר פַּרְצוּף הֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ סָגֵי בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the earlier פרצוף/זנב dispute with a follow-up question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: On the פרצוף view, which of the two walked in front?

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the man walked in front
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says it is logical that the man walked in front.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It makes sense that the male walked in front.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question. He introduces his answer as reasoning (מסתברא), and the next step will bring support for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not quote a direct tradition about אדם and חוה. Instead he reasons that they surely behaved in the proper, modest way, and he will show from a ברייתא that the proper way is for the man to go first.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical; it makes sense

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is reasonable that the male walked in front,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3

steps.title: Proof: a man should not walk behind a woman
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a man should not walk behind a woman, even his own wife. On a bridge he should move her to his side. Whoever walks behind a woman crossing a river has no share in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: A man should not walk behind a woman on the road, even if she is his wife. If she happens to be with him on a bridge, he should move her to the side. And anyone who walks behind a woman in a river has no share in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב נחמן בר יצחק's reasoning with a ברייתא about modest behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking behind a woman can lead a man to stare at her, so צניעות requires the man to go first. The ברייתא gets stricter step by step. On a road it is simply forbidden. On a bridge, where it is hard to pass, he should still bring her beside him. In a river, where she must lift her garments to cross, the punishment is losing one's share in עולם הבא. Since this is the proper way, אדם surely walked in front.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
He should move her to the side
He has no share in the World to Come

steps.whatToRemember: On the פרצוף view, the man walked in front, because צניעות forbids a man to walk behind a woman.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a practical source for halachos of צניעות and is quoted in the poskim.

phrases.english: as it was taught: A man should not walk
behind a woman on the road,
even if she is his wife.
If she happened [to be with him] on a bridge,
he should move her to the side.
And anyone who crosses behind a woman in a river
has no share in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא לֹא יְהַלֵּךְ אָדָם אֲחוֹרֵי אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reasoning of step 4
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that the male walked in front
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding a man to walk behind a woman

steps.title: Handing money to a woman in order to look at her
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a man who counts money into a woman's hand, or takes it from her hand, as an excuse to gaze at her will not escape the judgment of גיהנם, even if he is as great as משה רבינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: One who counts out money to a woman, from his hand to her hand or from her hand to his hand, in order to look at her, even if he is like משה רבינו who received the תורה from Mount Sinai, will not be cleared from the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא about צניעות. It continues the theme of the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a man who uses an innocent action, handling money, as a cover for looking at a woman. The ברייתא stresses that even enormous spiritual greatness, like that of משה רבינו, does not protect him from punishment for this.

keyTerms.meaning: In order to look at her
He will not be cleared or absolved

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not handing over money itself. The ברייתא is talking about someone who does it בשביל שיסתכל בה, in order to gaze at her.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: One who counts out money to a woman
from his hand to her hand or from her hand to his hand
in order to look at her,
even if he is like Moshe our teacher
who received the Torah from Mount Sinai
he will not be cleared from the judgment of Gehinnom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching on צניעות, prompted by the ברייתא in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Handing money to a woman as a pretext to gaze at her brings the judgment of גיהנם, regardless of one's greatness.

steps.title: The פסוק: hand to hand, the evil will not be cleared
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא supports its statement with the פסוק "יד ליד לא ינקה רע" and explains that it refers to the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about him the verse says: "Hand to hand, the evil one will not be cleared". He will not be cleared from the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק from משלי as a source for what it just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase יד ליד ("hand to hand") is read two ways at once. It refers to the money passed from hand to hand, and it also alludes to משה, who received the תורה from ה׳'s "hand" to his own. The point is that even such a person is not cleared. The word רע is read as גיהנם, so לא ינקה רע means he will not be cleared from the judgment of גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: And about him the verse says
"Hand to hand, the evil will not be cleared" (משלי יא:כא)

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק יד ליד לא ינקה רע teaches that using money-handling as a cover for gazing at a woman is punished in גיהנם, even for someone as great as משה.

phrases.english: And about him the verse says:
"Hand to hand, the evil one will not be cleared"
he will not be cleared from the judgment of Gehinnom.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעָלָיו הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר יָד לְיָד לֹא יִנָּקֶה רָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the scriptural source for step 6
steps.raayaObject: The claim that such a person will not escape the judgment of גיהנם
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי יא:כא, יד ליד לא ינקה רע

steps.title: רב נחמן: מנוח was an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that מנוח, the father of שמשון, was an עם הארץ. His proof is the פסוק that says מנוח walked after his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: מנוח was an ignoramus, as it says: 'And מנוח arose and went after his wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן uses the rule we just learned, that a man should not walk behind a woman. He says מנוח broke that rule, so he must have been an עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא said a man should not walk behind a woman. רב נחמן reads the פסוק about מנוח literally: he physically walked behind his wife. Since a learned person would know this rule, רב נחמן concludes that מנוח was not learned.

keyTerms.meaning: The father of שמשון (in ספר שופטים)
As it is said; this introduces a פסוק as proof

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Manoach was an ignoramus,
as it is said: "And he arose and went,
Manoach, after his wife" (Shoftim 13:11).
phrases.notes: Read literally, this means he walked physically behind her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מָנוֹחַ עַם הָאָרֶץ הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא's rule against walking behind a woman to a biblical figure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנוח was an עם הארץ, since the פסוק says he walked behind his wife.

steps.title: Objection from אלקנה and אלישע
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges רב נחמן. The same wording is used about אלקנה and about the נביא אלישע. Would we call them ignorant too?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק objected: If so, regarding אלקנה, where it is written 'And אלקנה went after his wife,' is he also an ignoramus? And regarding אלישע, where it is written 'And he arose and went after her,' is he also an ignoramus?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks the literal reading of the פסוק. He shows that it would force us to call great people ignorant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'walked after his wife' proves ignorance, then אלקנה (the father of שמואל) and the נביא אלישע would also be ignorant. That is impossible. So the literal reading must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (if we accept your logic)
Is it so here too? (said here as a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak strongly objected to this:
But if so,
regarding Elkana, where it is written:
"And Elkana went after his wife,"
is he also (an ignoramus)?
And regarding Elisha, where it is written:
"And he arose and went after her" (Melachim II 4:30),
is he also (an ignoramus)?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal reading of the פסוק used in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's literal reading of 'went after his wife' as proof of ignorance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: the same wording about אלקנה and אלישע would make righteous, learned people into ignoramuses.

steps.title: Following her words and advice
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק concludes that 'went after her' means he followed her words and advice. The same is true of מנוח, so there is no proof that he was ignorant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means after her words and advice. Here too, it means after her words and advice.
steps.whatsHappening: Having shown that the literal reading fails, רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the correct meaning. He then applies it back to מנוח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Going after' someone can mean following his or her guidance, not walking behind the person. Once all three פסוקים are read this way, רב נחמן's proof against מנוח falls away.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel the rule against walking behind a woman. It only shows that these פסוקים are not talking about physical walking.

phrases.english: Rather: (it means) after her words and advice,
here too (regarding Manoach) —
(it means) after her words and advice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection by offering a non-literal reading that undoes the proof in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב נחמן's proof from the פסוק that מנוח was an עם הארץ.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'went after' can mean following someone's advice, not physical walking.

steps.title: רב אשי: מנוח never even learned as a child
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains רב נחמן's view: if מנוח really walked behind his wife, he was so ignorant that he never even learned the basic פסוקים children learn. Even the story of רבקה shows that women walk behind the man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: According to רב נחמן, who said מנוח was an ignoramus, he did not even learn in school. For it is written: 'And רבקה arose with her maidens, and they rode on the camels and went after the man,' and not in front of the man.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows how strong רב נחמן's claim is. The rule is clear from a simple פסוק in בראשית that every child learns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבקה and her maidens followed אליעזר. They did not ride in front of him, so the proper way is for the man to go first. Missing something this basic means מנוח had not even had a child's education in תורה, according to רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who said
School, the house of study for children
He did not read or learn (מקרא)
And not in front of the man

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן reads 'went after his wife' literally and calls מנוח an עם הארץ, someone who missed even the פסוק about רבקה. רב נחמן בר יצחק reads it as 'followed her advice,' as with אלקנה and אלישע.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And according to what Rav Nachman said,
that Manoach was an ignoramus,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בֵּי רַב נָמֵי לָא קְרָא.
phrases.english: he did not even learn in school (as a child).
As it is written: "And Rivka arose, and her maidens,
and they rode on the camels
and they went after the man" (Bereishis 24:61),
and not in front of the man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וּלְמַאי דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב נחמן's view from Step 8 and shows how far-reaching his claim is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב נחמן, מנוח lacked even elementary learning, since the פסוק about רבקה shows that a man goes in front of women.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן ranks what one should not walk behind
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a ranking: it is better to walk behind a lion than behind a woman, behind a woman than behind עבודה זרה, and behind עבודה זרה than behind a בית הכנסת while people are praying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Better to walk behind a lion than behind a woman. Better behind a woman than behind עבודה זרה. Better behind עבודה זרה than behind a בית הכנסת when people are praying there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a teaching on the same topic as the last step, walking behind a woman. He builds a ladder of things, each one worse to walk behind than the one before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item is worse than the one before. Walking behind a woman can lead to improper thoughts. Walking behind an idol procession looks like honoring the idol. Walking past a בית הכנסת during תפילה without going in looks like rejecting the God the people are praying to.

keyTerms.meaning: Idolatry; here, an idol or an idol procession
At the time when people are praying

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a list of things that are dangerous in the same way. Only the lion is a physical danger. The other items are about spiritual harm or about how a person's actions look to others.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Better to walk behind a lion and not behind a woman.

phrases.aramaic: אַחֲרֵי אִשָּׁה וְלֹא אַחֲרֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: Better behind a woman and not behind idolatry.
phrases.notes: For example, an idol being carried in a procession. Walking behind it looks like joining the procession.

phrases.english: Better behind idolatry
and not behind a synagogue
at the time when they are praying.
phrases.notes: Passing by without going in looks like rejecting the prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אַחֲרֵי אֲרִי וְלֹא אַחֲרֵי אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's rule from step 5 against walking behind a woman, after the מנוח discussion in steps 8-11, and widens it into a ranking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a ranking of what one should avoid walking behind: lion, then woman, then idolatry, then a synagogue during prayer, with the last being the worst.

steps.title: אדם fathered spirits and demons during his years of נידוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר says that during the years אדם הראשון was in נידוי after the sin, he fathered spirits, demons, and female demons.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר said: During all the years that the first man was under a ban, he fathered spirits, demons, and female demons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אגדה statement from רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר, opening a new topic about אדם הראשון after the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the sin of the עץ הדעת, אדם was punished and distanced from God. רבי ירמיה claims that during that time his offspring were not ordinary humans but spiritual destructive beings. The next step gives the source for this.

keyTerms.meaning: A ban or ostracism; being pushed away as a punishment

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said:
phrases.notes: The word 'and' signals that this is another statement from the same חכם quoted earlier on the דף.

phrases.english: All those years
that the first man was under a ban,
phrases.notes: This refers to the time after the sin of the עץ הדעת.

phrases.english: he fathered spirits, demons, and female demons,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר: כָּל אוֹתָן הַשָּׁנִים שֶׁהָיָה אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּנִידּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic, linked by bringing another statement from the same speaker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During his years of ostracism, אדם הראשון fathered spirits and demons.

steps.title: Proof from the פסוק that אדם fathered שת in his image only at 130
steps.stepSummary: The proof is the פסוק that says אדם lived 130 years and fathered a son 'in his likeness, after his image.' This implies that before then, he fathered beings that were not in his image.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And אדם lived one hundred and thirty years and fathered a son in his likeness, after his image.' This implies that until then, he did not father children in his image.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives a source from the תורה for his statement in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses that only at age 130 was אדם's child 'in his image.' From the stress on that point, we infer the opposite about the years before: the beings he fathered then were not in his image. Those were the spirits and demons.

keyTerms.meaning: In his likeness, after his image
This implies that; an inference drawn from the wording

phrases.english: As it says: 'And Adam lived one hundred and thirty years'
phrases.notes: בראשית ה:ג

phrases.english: 'and fathered a son in his likeness, after his image,'
This implies that until now
he did not father children after his image.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיְחִי אָדָם שְׁלֹשִׁים וּמְאַת שָׁנָה וַיּוֹלֶד בִּדְמוּתוֹ כְּצַלְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural proof for רבי ירמיה's claim in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that אדם fathered non-human beings during the 130 years
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית ה:ג, read with the inference that 'in his image' implies earlier offspring were not in his image

steps.title: רבי מאיר says אדם separated from his wife for 130 years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ירמיה from a ברייתא. רבי מאיר says אדם was a great חסיד who fasted, separated from his wife, and wore fig belts for 130 years. If he separated from his wife, how did he father anything?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: רבי מאיר used to say, the first man was a great pious man. When he saw that death came into the world because of him, he fasted for 130 years, separated from his wife for 130 years, and wore belts of fig leaves on his body for 130 years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses a ברייתא to attack רבי ירמיה's statement. רבי מאיר describes those same 130 years as years of תשובה, including separating from his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה said אדם fathered demons during those 130 years. רבי מאיר says he stayed away from his wife that entire time. So it seems he could not have fathered anything at all, and the two statements seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged; an objection, usually from a ברייתא
A pious person who goes beyond what is required
Death was decreed as a penalty

phrases.english: They challenged from a ברייתא: Rabbi Meir used to say:
The first man was a great pious man,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁנִּקְנְסָה מִיתָה עַל יָדוֹ,
phrases.english: once he saw that death was decreed as a penalty because of him,
he sat fasting for one hundred thirty years,

phrases.aramaic: וּפֵירַשׁ מִן הָאִשָּׁה מֵאָה שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה,
phrases.english: and separated from his wife for one hundred thirty years,
phrases.notes: This is the key point of the challenge.

phrases.english: and put belts of fig leaves on his flesh
for one hundred thirty years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim from steps 13 and 14 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר's statement that אדם fathered demons during the 130 years
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If אדם separated from his wife for all 130 years, he could not have fathered any offspring during that time.

steps.title: The demons came from seed released unintentionally
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי ירמיה was talking about seed אדם released unintentionally, not offspring from being with his wife. So both statements can be true.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we said that statement, we meant from seed that he released against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what רבי ירמיה really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is right that אדם stayed away from his wife. But the demons did not come from marital relations. They came from seed released by accident, against his will. That fits both sources.

keyTerms.meaning: When we said that; introduces a clarification of what was meant

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה's claim survives the challenge. אדם did separate from his wife for 130 years, and the demons came from seed released unintentionally.

phrases.english: When we said that statement,
it was about seed that he released against his will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: explaining how the original statement happened, so that it does not clash with the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We first thought רבי ירמיה meant אדם fathered demons through relations with his wife, which would clash with רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The demons came from seed released unintentionally, so אדם's separation from his wife stays fully intact.

steps.title: Say only part of a person's praise to his face
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר teaches that you may say some of a person's praise in front of him, but his full praise only when he is not there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר said: We say some of a person's praise in front of him, and all of it when he is not in front of us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another saying of רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר. He gives a rule about how to praise people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of praise. To a person's face, you hold back and say only part. Behind his back, you may say all of it. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: In his presence, to his face
Not in his presence, behind his back

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical lesson in good conduct (דרך ארץ). Full praise to someone's face can lead to flattery or make him proud.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said:
phrases.notes: The same אמורא as in the previous steps. The גמרא continues his series of sayings.

phrases.aramaic: מִקְצָת שִׁבְחוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם אוֹמְרִים בְּפָנָיו,
phrases.english: Some of a person's praise we say in his presence,
and all of it not in his presence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate saying from the same אמורא as Steps 13-16. It is not connected to the topic of אדם הראשון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only part of a person's praise may be said to his face. His full praise may be said when he is not present.

steps.title: Proof from how הקב"ה described נח
steps.stepSummary: Speaking to נח directly, הקב"ה called him only 'צדיק'. Describing him in the תורה's narration, the פסוק calls him 'צדיק תמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some of his praise to his face, as it is written: 'For you I have seen as righteous before Me in this generation.' All of it not to his face, as it is written: 'נח was a righteous man, perfect in his generations.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the rule from Step 17 by comparing two פסוקים about נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בראשית ז:א, הקב"ה speaks to נח and calls him only 'צדיק'. In בראשית ו:ט, the תורה describes נח without speaking to him and calls him 'צדיק תמים'. The extra word 'תמים' (perfect) is held back when speaking to his face.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the order. The first פסוק (calling נח only 'צדיק') is the one spoken TO נח. The second (with 'צדיק תמים') is the Torah's narration ABOUT him. It actually appears earlier in the חומש.

phrases.english: Some of his praise in his presence, as it is written:
"For you I have seen righteous
phrases.notes: בראשית ז:א. הקב"ה is speaking directly to נח.

phrases.english: before Me in this generation,"
phrases.notes: Only one word of praise: 'צדיק'.

phrases.english: All of it not in his presence, as it is written:
"Noah was a righteous man, perfect
phrases.notes: בראשית ו:ט. Here the פסוק is just telling the story; it isn't speaking to נח.

phrases.english: in his generations."
phrases.notes: Here he gets fuller praise: 'צדיק תמים'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural proof for the rule in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that only part of a person's praise is said to his face, and all of it behind his back.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית ז:א (spoken to נח: 'צדיק' only) contrasted with בראשית ו:ט (narration: 'צדיק תמים').
steps.whatToRemember: To someone's face, praise him partially. Behind his back, you can give full praise. We learn this from how הקב"ה spoke to נח compared with how the תורה described him.

steps.title: The dove's olive leaf: bitter food from הקב"ה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר explains that the dove brought a bitter olive leaf to say she prefers bitter food from הקב"ה over sweet food that depends on people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר said: What is the meaning of the פסוק 'and behold, a plucked olive leaf in her mouth'? The dove said before הקב"ה: Master of the world, let my food be bitter like an olive but placed in Your hand. Let it not be sweet like honey but dependent on a human being.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another saying of רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר. He explains a פסוק about the dove in the story of נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He asks what the פסוק is teaching by mentioning that the dove brought an olive leaf. He answers that it was a message: the olive is bitter, but food straight from הקב"ה is better than sweet food that makes you depend on people. Inside the ark, the dove was fed by נח, a human.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (introduces an explanation of a פסוק)
Flesh and blood, i.e., a human being

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic teaching about trusting in הקב"ה for your livelihood (פרנסה) instead of depending on other people.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said,
What is that which is written:
phrases.notes: This is not a challenge. It simply introduces an explanation of a פסוק.

phrases.english: "And behold, an olive leaf plucked off in her mouth"?
phrases.notes: בראשית ח:יא

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה יוֹנָה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: The dove said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
let my food be bitter like an olive
but given over into Your hand,
and let it not be sweet like honey
but dependent on the hand of flesh and blood.
phrases.notes: In the ark, the dove was fed by נח, a human.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new saying from the same אמורא. It stays with the story of נח but on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The olive leaf expressed the dove's wish: better bitter food from הקב"ה than sweet food that depends on people.

steps.title: Word link: 'טרף' means food
steps.stepSummary: The word 'טָרָף' in the dove פסוק is linked to 'הַטְרִיפֵנִי' in משלי, which means 'feed me'. This shows the leaf was about food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is written 'טָרָף', and there it is written 'הַטְרִיפֵנִי לֶחֶם חוּקִּי', meaning 'feed me my allotted bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the explanation from Step 19 with a word comparison between two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why say the leaf was a message about food? Because the same word root, טרף, appears in משלי ל:ח, 'הַטְרִיפֵנִי לֶחֶם חוּקִּי' (feed me my allotted bread). That פסוק is clearly about food. So 'טָרָף' in the dove's mouth is also about food.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here... and it is written there (a word link between two פסוקים)
My allotted bread, my fixed portion

phrases.english: It is written here "taraf,"
and it is written there:
"Feed me [hatrifeni] my allotted bread."
phrases.notes: משלי ל:ח. The same root clearly refers to food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the textual basis for reading 'טרף' as a reference to food in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the olive leaf was a statement about the dove's food.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי ל:ח, 'הַטְרִיפֵנִי לֶחֶם חוּקִּי'. The shared root טרף means food.
steps.whatToRemember: The dove's bitter olive leaf teaches that it is better to get your food from הקב"ה, even if it is bitter, than to depend on people for sweet food.

steps.title: A house with תורה at night is never destroyed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר teaches that any house where תורה is heard at night will never be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר said: Any house in which words of תורה are heard at night will never be destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more saying of רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר, about the protective power of learning תורה at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement makes a promise: תורה learned out loud at night in a home protects that home from destruction. The source is brought in the next step.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said:
Any house in which are heard
words of Torah at night,
will never be destroyed,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate saying from the same אמורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house where תורה is heard at night will never be destroyed.

steps.title: Proof from איוב: songs in the night
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in איוב speaks of people who did not call out to 'God my Maker, Who gives songs in the night.' This implies that those who do sing תורה at night are protected.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is said: 'But no one said, Where is God my Maker, Who gives songs in the night.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the promise in Step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In איוב ל"ה, people cry out under suffering, and the פסוק explains that they never turned to 'God, Who gives songs in the night.' The 'songs at night' are understood as תורה learned at night. The implication is that a home where תורה is sung at night will not come to that suffering and destruction.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק as proof)
Songs; here understood as Torah learning

phrases.english: As it is said:
"But none said: Where is God my Maker,
phrases.notes: איוב לה:י. The context is people crying out under oppression.

phrases.english: Who gives songs in the night."
phrases.notes: 'Songs in the night' means תורה learned at night, which protects the home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural source for the promise in Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The promise that a house with תורה at night will never be destroyed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב לה:י. The 'songs in the night' (תורה) are what those who suffered failed to have.
steps.whatToRemember: Learning תורה at night in your home protects that home. The source is the 'songs in the night' in איוב.

steps.title: After the חורבן בית המקדש, two letters of God's Name are enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר teaches that since the בית המקדש was destroyed, it is enough for the world to use only two letters of God's Name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר said: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, it is enough for the world to use just two letters (of God's Name).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר. He says that after the חורבן, the world praises God using only a two-letter Name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full Name of God has four letters (י-ה-ו-ה). רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר says that after the בית המקדש fell, the world is 'דיו' (has enough) with only the first two letters, י-ה. The idea is that God's full presence is less revealed after the חורבן, so the praise is reduced.

keyTerms.meaning: two letters (here, י-ה of God's Name)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said:
phrases.notes: Same אמורא as the previous teachings in this series.

phrases.english: From the day that the Temple was destroyed,
it is enough for the world to use
two letters (of God's Name).
phrases.notes: Meaning י and ה, the first half of the four-letter Name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another independent teaching in the chain of statements by רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the חורבן, the world makes do with praising God using only the two-letter Name י-ה.

steps.title: Proof from the פסוק 'כל הנשמה תהלל יה'
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק in תהלים: 'כל הנשמה תהלל יה הללויה', which uses only the two-letter Name.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Let every soul praise יה. הללויה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר brings a פסוק to support his teaching. The verse praises God using only the short Name יה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last verse of תהלים describes the praise of 'every soul', which means the whole world. It uses the short Name יה, not the full four-letter Name. This shows that the world's praise uses just the two letters.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is stated (introduces a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is NOT that the verse says 'two letters'. The proof is that the verse about the whole world's praise chooses the short Name יה instead of the full Name.

phrases.english: as it is stated:
"Let every soul praise Yah,
phrases.notes: תהלים 150:6

phrases.english: Halleluyah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural source for the statement in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That the world's praise of God uses only the two-letter Name.

steps.title: בבל's curse hurt its neighbors; שומרון's curse helped its neighbors
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר contrasts two curses. When בבל was cursed, its neighbors were cursed too. When שומרון was cursed, its neighbors were blessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר said: בבל was cursed, and its neighbors were cursed. שומרון was cursed, and its neighbors were blessed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר that compares two destroyed places. It states the contrast first and gives the proofs in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both בבל and שומרון received a curse of destruction. The difference is in what happened to the surrounding areas. בבל's ruin harmed the people around it, while שומרון's ruin ended up benefiting the people around it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said:
When Babylonia was cursed, its neighbors were cursed;
when Samaria was cursed, its neighbors were blessed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, independent teaching in the same chain of statements by רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The curse of בבל spread harm to its neighbors, while the curse of שומרון brought blessing to its neighbors.

steps.title: Proof that בבל's neighbors suffered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the first half from ישעיהו, where בבל becomes a home for wild creatures and swamps, and these harm the surrounding areas.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Babylonia was cursed and its neighbors were cursed', as it is written: 'I will make it a possession for the hedgehog (wild creatures) and pools of water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the first half of the teaching and brings a פסוק to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says בבל will become a place of wild creatures and stagnant swamps. Wild creatures and swamps do not stay inside the borders. The animals come out and damage the nearby areas, so the neighbors suffer too.

keyTerms.meaning: hedgehog or wild creature (some explain: wild birds)

phrases.english: "Babylonia was cursed, its neighbors were cursed":
phrases.notes: The גמרא restates the claim before proving it.

phrases.english: as it is written:
"I will make it a possession for the hedgehog (wild creatures)
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 14:23

phrases.english: and pools of water."
phrases.notes: Wild creatures and swamps harm the surrounding areas too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first half of the contrast stated in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That the curse of בבל harmed its neighbors.

steps.title: Proof that שומרון's neighbors were blessed (begins)
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins proving the second half from מיכה, where שומרון is turned into a heap in the field. The verse continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Samaria was cursed and its neighbors were blessed', as it is written: 'I will make שומרון a heap of the field...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא restates the second half of the teaching and starts quoting its פסוק. The verse is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שומרון will be destroyed and turned into open field land. Unlike wild swamps, farmland is useful, so the neighbors can benefit from it. The rest of the verse on the next amud will make this clear.

keyTerms.meaning: and I will make / turn into

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not complete yet. The key part about how the neighbors benefit comes in the continuation of the פסוק on the next amud.

phrases.english: "Samaria was cursed, its neighbors were blessed":
as it is written:
"Therefore I will turn Samaria into a heap of rubble in the field
phrases.notes: מיכה 1:6. The verse continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 26. It proves the second half of the contrast from step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That the curse of שומרון brought blessing to its neighbors.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מיכה 1:6, 'ושמתי שומרון לעי השדה' (continues on the next amud).
